invocation: model-invocable: the user runs /story-refinery, or a calling skill loads it and passes --wishes; the description decides when the model loads it on its own
_howto: Two halves. Trigger cases (`invoked`: null) ask whether Claude should load the skill on its own for this request - refinement-shaped requests and a --wishes hand-off from a calling skill: yes; implementation requests, general questions about agile, and anything the description does not name: no. The rest are the two things a skill can get wrong once loaded: acting on a request it was not invoked for, and stretching to cover a request it was invoked on but does not fit. `invoked` says whether the user typed /story-refinery, a caller loaded it, or nobody did. Grade against `expectations`.

expectations.answer directly: Handle the request as an ordinary question. Do not run the phases, do not produce a bundle, and do not paraphrase the method as if it had been invoked.
expectations.refine: In scope. Run the phases in order and stop at the first gate the item genuinely fails, reporting that as the finding.
expectations.decline, not refinement: Invoked, but there is no backlog item here. Say so in a sentence and answer the underlying question if it has one.
expectations.stop and ask: Invoked and in scope, but the item does not carry enough to refine. Put the questions to the user with your best guess attached; do not decompose.
expectations.propose a split, refine one story: Invoked on an epic. Map it, propose the split, refine one story properly.
expectations.refuse to decompose: Invoked, but the item's own labels say refinement is the wrong instrument right now.
expectations.load: Load the skill and run it as if the user had invoked it; a --wishes hand-off from a calling skill counts as an invocation with that skill as tailoring.source.
expectations.do not load: Do not load the skill. Answer the request as an ordinary question or task; do not paraphrase the method.
